norse.text: Þórr fór ór Austrvegi ok kom at sundi einu. Öðrum megin sundsins var ferjukarlinn með skipit. Þórr kallaði:

"Hverr er sá sveinn sveina,
er stendr fyr sundit handan?"

"Hverr er sá karl karla,
er kallar of váginn?"

"Árligum verkum
hrósar þú, verðinum;
veizt-at-tu fyrir görla,
döpr eru þín heimkynni,
dauð, hygg ek, at þín móðir sé."

"Þat segir þú nú,
er hverjum þykkir
mest at vita,
at mín móðir dauð sé."

"Þeygi er sem þú
þrjú bú góð eigir;
berbeinn þú stendr
ok hefr brautinga gervi,
þatki, at þú hafir brækr þínar."

"Stýrðu hingat eikjunni,
ek mun þér stöðna kenna, -
eða hverr á skipit,
er þú heldr við landit?"

"Hildolfr sá heitir,
er mik halda bað,
rekkr inn ráðsvinni,
er býr í Ráðseyjarsundi;
bað-at hann hlennimenn flytja
eða hrossaþjófa,
góða eina
ok þá, er ek görva kunna;
segðu til nafns þíns,
ef þú vill um sundit fara!"

"Segja mun ek til nafns míns,
þótt ek sekr séak,
ok til alls eðlis:
Ek em Óðins sonr,
Meila bróðir,
en Magna faðir,
þrúðvaldr goða,
við Þór knáttu hér dæma!
Hins vil ek nú spyrja,
hvat þú heitir."

"Hárbarðr ek heiti,
hylk um nafn sjaldan."

"Hvat skaltu of nafn hylja,
nema þú sakar eigir?"

"En þótt ek sakar eiga,
þá mun ek forða fjörvi mínu
fyr slíkum sem þú ert,
nema ek feigr sé."

"Harm ljótan
mér þykkir í því
at vaða um váginn til þín
ok væta ögur minn;
skylda ek launa
kögursveini þínum
kanginyrði,
ef ek kæmumk yfir sundit."

"Hér mun ek standa
ok þín heðan bíða;
fannt-a þú mann in harðara
at Hrungni dauðan."

"Hins viltu nú geta,
er vit Hrungnir deildum,
sá inn stórúðgi jötunn,
er ór steini var höfuðit á;
þó lét ek hann falla
ok fyrir hníga.
Hvat vanntu þá meðan, Hárbarðr?"

"Var ek með Fjölvari
fimm vetr alla
í ey þeiri,
er Algræn heitir;
vega vér þar knáttum
ok val fella,
margs at freista,
mans at kosta."

"Ek drap Þjaza,
inn þrúðmóðga jötun,
upp ek varp augum
Alvalda sonar
á þann inn heiða himin;
þau eru merki mest
minna verka,
þau er allir menn síðan of séa.
Hvat vanntu þá meðan, Hárbarðr?"

"Miklar manvélar
ek hafða við myrkriður,
þá er ek vélta þær frá verum;
harðan jötun
ek hugða Hlébarð vera,
gaf hann mér gambantein,
en ek vélta hann ór viti."

"Illum huga
launaðir þú þá góðar gjafar."

"Þat hefr eik,
er af annarri skefr,
of sik er hverr í slíku.
Hvat vanntu þá meðan Þórr?"

"Ek var austr
ok jötna barðak
brúðir bölvísar,
er til bjargs gengu;
mikil myndi ætt jötna,
ef allir lifði
vætr myndi manna
undir Miðgarði.
Hvat vanntu þá meðan, Hárbarðr?"

"Var ek á Vallandi
ok vígum fylgdak,
atta ek jöfrum,
en aldri sættak;
Óðinn á jarla,
þá er í val falla,
en Þórr á þrælakyn."

"Ójafnt skipta
er þú myndir með ásum liði,
ef þú ættir vilgi mikils vald."

"Þórr á afl ærit,
en ekki hjarta;
af hræðslu ok hugbleyði
þér var í hanzka troðit,
ok þóttisk-a þú þá Þórr vera;
hvárki þú þá þorðir
fyr hræðslu þinni
hnjósa né físa,
svá at Fjalarr heyrði."

"Hárbarðr inn ragi,
ek mynda þik í hel drepa,
ef ek mætta seilask um sund."

"Hvat skyldir um sund seilask,
er sakir ro alls engar?
Hvat vanntu þá, Þórr?"

"Ek var austr
ok ána varðak,
þá er mik sóttu
þeir Svárangs synir;
grjóti þeir mik börðu,
gagni urðu þeir þó lítt fegnir,
þó urðu þeir mik fyrri
friðar at biðja.
Hvat vanntu þá meðan, Hárbarðr?"

"Ek var austr
ok við einhverja dæmðak,
lék ek við ina línhvítu
ok launþing háðak;
gladdak ina gullbjörtu,
gamni mær unði."
"Góð átt þú þér mankynni þar þá."

"Liðs þíns
væra ek þá þurfi, Þórr,
at ek helda þeiri inni línhvítu mey."

"Ek munda þér þá þat veita,
ef ek viðr of kæmumk."

"Ek mynda þér þá trúa,
nema þú mik í tryggð véltir."

"Emk-at ek sá hælbítr
sem húðskór forn á vár."

"Brúðir berserkja
barðak í Hléseyju;
þær höfðu verst unnit,
vélta þjóð alla."

"Klæki vanntu þá, Þórr,
er þú á konum barðir."

"Vargynjur þat váru,
en varla konur,
skelldu skip mitt,
er ek skorðat hafðak,
ægðu mér járnlurki
en eltu Þjalfa.
Hvat vanntu meðan, Hárbarðr?"

"Ek vark í hernum,
er hingat gerðisk
gnæfa gunnfana,
geir at rjóða."

"Þess viltu nú geta,
er þú fórt oss óljúfan at bjóða."

"Bæta skal þér þat þá
munda baugi,
sem jafnendr unnu,
þeir er okkr vilja sætta."

"Hvar namtu þessi
in hnæfiligu orð,
er ek heyrða aldregi
in hnæfiligri?"

"Nam ek at mönnum
þeim inum aldrænum,
er búa í heimis skógum."

"Þó gefr þú gott nafn dysjum,
er þú kallar þær heimis skóga."

"Orðkringi þín
mun þér illa koma,
ef ek ræð á vág at vaða;
ulfi hæra
hygg ek þik æpa munu,
ef þú hlýtr af hamri högg."

"Sif á hó heima,
hans muntu fund vilja,
þann muntu þrek drýgja,
þat er þér skyldara."

"Mælir þú at munns ráði,
svá at mér skyldi verst þykkja,
halr inn hugblauði,
hygg ek, at þú ljúgir."

"Satt hygg ek mik segja;
seinn ertu at för þinni,
langt myndir þú nú kominn, Þórr,
ef þú litum færir."

"Hárbarðr inn ragi,
heldr hefr þú nú mik dvalðan."

"Ása-þórs hugða ek
aldregi mundu
glepja féhirði farar."

"Ráð mun ek þér nú ráða;
ró þú hingat bátinum,
hættum hætingi,
hittu föður Magna."

"Farðu firr sundi,
þér skal fars synja."

"Vísa þú mér nú leiðina,
alls þú vill mik eigi um váginn ferja."

Lítit er at synja,
langt er at fara;
stund er til stokksins,
önnur til steinsins,
haltu svá til vinstra vegsins,
unz þú hittir Verland;
þar mun Fjörgyn
hitta Þór, son sinn,
ok mun hon kenna hánum áttunga brautir
til Óðins landa."

"Taka við víl ok erfiði,
at upprennandi sólu,
er ek get þána."

"Skammt mun nú mál okkat,
alls þú mér skætingu einni svarar;
launa mun ek þér farsynjun,
ef vit finnumk í sinn annat."

"Far þú nú,
þars þik hafi allan gramir."

english.text: Thor was on his way back from a journey in the East, and came to a sound; on the other side of the sound was a ferryman with a boat. Thor called out:
"Who is the fellow yonder, | on the farther shore of the sound?"
"What kind of a peasant is yon, | that calls o'er the bay?"

"Of thy morning feats art thou proud, | but the future thou knowest not wholly;
Doleful thine home-coming is: | thy mother, me thinks, is dead."

"Now hast thou said | what to each must seem
The mightiest grief, | that my mother is dead."

"Steer thou hither the boat; | the landing here shall I show thee;
But whose the craft | that thou keepest on the shore?"

"Hildolf is he | who bade me have it,
A hero wise; | his home is at Rathsey's sound.
He bade me no robbers to steer, | nor stealers of steeds,
But worthy men, | and those whom well do I know.
Say now thy name, | if over the sound thou wilt fare."

"My name indeed shall I tell, | though in danger I am,
And all my race; | I am Othin's son,
Meili's brother, | and Magni's father,
The strong one of the gods; | with Thor now speech canst thou get.
And now would I know | what name thou hast."
"Harbarth am I, | and seldom I hide my name."
"Why shouldst thou hide thy name, | if quarrel thou hast not?"

"And though I had a quarrel, | from such as thou art
Yet none the less | my life would I guard,
Unless I be doomed to die."

"Great trouble, methinks, | would it be to come to thee,
To wade the waters across, | and wet my middle;
Weakling, well shall I pay | thy mocking words,
if across the sound I come."

"Here shall I stand | and await thee here;
Thou hast found since Hrungnir died | no fiercer man."

"Fain art thou to tell | how with Hrungnir I fought,
The haughty giant, | whose head of stone was made;
And yet I felled him, | and stretched him before me.
What, Harbarth, didst thou the while?"

"Five full winters | with Fjolvar was I,
And dwelt in the isle | that is Algrön called;
There could we fight, | and fell the slain,
Much could we seek, | and maids could master."
"How won ye success with your women?"

"Lively women we had, | if they wise for us were;
Wise were the women we had, | if they kind for us were;
For ropes of sand | they would seek to wind,
And the bottom to dig | from the deepest dale.
Wiser than all | in counsel I was,
And there I slept | by the sisters seven,
And joy full great | did I get from each.
What, Thor, didst thou the while?"

"Thjazi I felled, | the giant fierce,
And I hurled the eyes | of Alvaldi's son
To the heavens hot above;
Of my deeds the mightiest | marks are these,
That all men since can see.
What, Harbarth, didst thou the while?"
Harbarth spoke:

"Much love-craft I wrought | with them who ride by night,
When I stole them by stealth from their husbands;
A giant hard | was Hlebarth, methinks:
His wand he gave me as gift,
And I stole his wits away."
"Thou didst repay good gifts with evil mind."

"In Valland I was, | and wars I raised,
Princes I angered, | and peace brought never;
The noble who fall | in the fight hath Othin,
And Thor hath the race of the thralls."

"Unequal gifts | of men wouldst thou give to the gods,
If might too much thou shouldst have."

"Thou womanish Harbarth, | to hell would I smite thee straight,
Could mine arm reach over the sound."

"Wherefore reach over the sound, | since strife we have none?
What, Thor, didst thou do then?"
"Thy help did I need then, Thor, | to hold the white maid fast."
"Gladly, had I been there, | my help to thee had been given."
"I might have trusted thee then, | didst thou not betray thy troth."

"No heel-biter am I, in truth, | like an old leather shoe in spring."
Harbarth spoke:

"In Hlesey the brides | of the Berserkers slew I;
Most evil they were, | and all they betrayed."
"Shame didst thou win, | that women thou slewest, Thor."

"In the host I was | that hither fared,
The banners to raise, | and the spear to redden."
"Wilt thou now say | that hatred thou soughtest to bring us?"

"A ring for thy hand | shall make all right for thee,
As the judge decides | who sets us two at peace."

"Where foundest thou | so foul and scornful a speech?
More foul a speech | I never before have heard."

"I learned it from men, | the men so old,
Who dwell in the hills of home."

"A name full good | to heaps of stones thou givest
When thou callest them hills of home."

"Ill for thee comes | thy keenness of tongue,
If the water I choose to wade;
Louder, I ween, | than a wolf thou cryest,
If a blow of my hammer thou hast."

"Sif has a lover at home, | and him shouldst thou meet;
More fitting it were | on him to put forth thy strength."

"Thy tongue still makes thee say | what seems most ill to me,
Thou witless man! Thou liest, I ween."

"Truth do I speak, | but slow on thy way thou art;
Far hadst thou gone | if now in the boat thou hadst fared."
"Thou womanish Harbarth! | here hast thou held me too long."

"I thought not ever | that Asathor would be hindered
By a ferryman thus from faring."

"One counsel I bring thee now: | row hither thy boat;
No more of scoffing; | set Magni's father across."
"From the sound go hence; | the passage thou hast not."
"The way now show me, since thou takest me not o'er the water."
"May I come so far in a day?"

"With toil and trouble perchance,
While the sun still shines, or so I think."

"Short now shall be our speech, for thou speakest in mockery only;
The passage thou gavest me not I shall pay thee if ever we meet."
"Get hence where every evil thing shall have thee!"
